findings_qualitative.value: ALMA continuum shows finger-like features (3500-10000 AU) around a dusty envelope (~18000 AU) with embedded sources.

evidence.quote: The ALMA 1.16 mm continuum map shows multiple finger-like features (extent $\sim$3500–10000 AU) surrounding a dusty envelope-like feature (extent $\sim$18000 AU)

claims.hypothesis: Does G11P1 host two velocity components at small scale?
claims.experiment: ALMA H13CO+(3-2) spectra, PV diagrams and moment maps toward the envelope
claims.result: Two peaks near 29 and 31 km/s, separation ~2 km/s
claims.finding: Small-scale two-component structure consistent with large-scale components, suggesting collision

evidence.quote: The ALMA H$^{13}$CO$^{+}$ line data show two cloud components with a velocity separation of $\sim$2 km s$^{-1}$ toward G11P1.

claims.result: Four IR-dark HFS candidates plus G11P1-HFS

evidence.quote: Hence, the infrared observations reveal multiple infrared-dark HFS candidates at multi-scale in G11.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: No complementary distribution of the two clouds was found, which does not favour a simple cloud-cloud collision signature

evidence.quote: The analysis of the molecular line data does not favour the presence of any complementary distribution of two clouds in our target area.

limitations_admitted.value: Sub-filaments and HFS candidates need higher-resolution observations to validate

evidence.quote: to validate the existence of sub-filaments and IR-dark HFS candidates, we require new continuum and line observations (resolution $<$ 2$''$)

referee_caveats_inferred: HFS and collision identification is largely visual
Velocity separation of 2 km/s is small for collision claims
